summary: In bad(), the array index `data` is set to -1 and then used to read `array[data]` without any bounds check, causing an out-of-bounds (negative index) read. I added a bounds check that validates the index is within `[0, array.length)` before using it to index the array, mirroring the standard fix of guarding the access against the known array size. Valid (in-range) indices continue to work and print the selected element; an out-of-range index is simply not used for the read.
